evals.name: torch-leak-and-mutable-trajectory
evals.prompt: I just wrote the first version of the core primitives in latent_space_bad.py for latent-anything. Can you review it before I commit it?
evals.expected_output: FAIL verdict. Catches torch.Tensor in the public whiten() signature (must be numpy), the in-place mutating Trajectory.append (Trajectory must be immutable), interpolate() hardcoding euclidean lerp instead of geometry dispatch, and LatentSpace keyed on shape instead of geometry. Each finding cites file:line + the rule/ADR.

evals.name: premature-method-protocol
evals.prompt: I'm adding UMAP as the second introspection method and pulled out a shared Method interface in methods.py. Is this good and compliant with how we build latent-anything?
evals.expected_output: Flags premature abstraction: a Method Protocol was frozen with only 2 concrete implementations (PCA, UMAP); Rule of Three says extract the interface only at the 3rd differing-philosophy instance (SAE), keep a tentative unstable shape until then, and not on the public surface. Cites INCREMENTAL.md §4a.

evals.name: clean-narrow-trajectory
evals.prompt: Review my Trajectory implementation in trajectory.py before I commit it.
evals.expected_output: PASS or PASS-WITH-WARNINGS. Recognizes immutability is correct, numpy public surface is correct, and does NOT falsely flag the euclidean-only scope as an ADR violation (narrow is allowed — only making the general shape impossible is a violation). Advisory notes (e.g. missing tests/changelog) are fine.
